name: Twin Bars
description: On headphones each key strikes two bars a few hertz apart, one nearer each ear, so every note beats at one rate from the lowest key to the highest.

params.name: Beat
params.description: How many hertz apart the two bars of a key are, on every overtone. That is the rate of the beat, the same on a low key as on a high one. Ringing bars follow it.

params.name: Ears
params.description: At 1 each ear has one bar and the beat is made between the ears. At 0 both bars sit in the middle. Speakers, a mono fold or a shared reverb give a beat in the air.

params.name: Bar
params.description: What the bars are made of. Metal rings long and bright, wood knocks and leaves a short hum, glass is close to a pure tone. Heard from the next key.

params.name: Mallet
params.description: How hard the mallet is. Soft gives a round start with few overtones, hard gives a bright knock. Heard from the next strike.

params.name: Decay
params.description: How long a held key rings: the time its low tone takes to fall 60 dB, on any key. Overtones die sooner, far sooner on wood.

params.name: Scatter
params.description: Strikes the second bar of a key this much later than the first, so the pair flams and the beat starts at another place in its swing. Heard from the next strike.

params.name: Damp
params.description: How quickly the bars stop once a key is let go. At 0 they ring on as if held, at 1 they are stopped within a tenth of a second.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Tilts the overtones against the low tone, from dark and round to bright and thin. The low tone stays as loud.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Overall output level of the instrument.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit and cpp/kit/beat.h (the Ears law), a sibling of Mallets: each bar mode is a rotating complex one pole, and a key is two such bars whose every mode is a whole Beat apart, so the pair's low tones sit half of Beat either side of the key. The higher bar is the one nearer the left ear. Each key's beat starts at its own strike: there is no clock shared between keys. Mode ratios follow the acoustics of bars as textbooks give them: an uncut metal bar at 1 : 2.757 : 5.404 : 8.933 and a carved wooden bar at 1 : 4 : 9.9. Choices, not measurements of an instrument: the glass ratios (1 : 2.32 : 4.25 : 6.63) and its faint overtones; the level of each mode; how much sooner an overtone dies than the low tone (the ring time is Decay over 1 plus a damping times the ratio less one: 0.25 for metal, 0.6 for glass, 3 for wood); Decay as the same time on every key, where a real bar rings shorter the higher it is; the mallet's contact time (2.5 ms soft to 0.25 ms hard at middle C, shorter up the keyboard and with a harder press); Damp as a power of 0.07 s over Decay, so 1 stops any bar in a tenth of a second; Tone's tilt of 1.5 down and 0.5 up per unit of log ratio. Simplified: the mallet is a raised cosine push with no thud or noise of its own, and it is divided by its own spectrum at the low tone so that Mallet changes colour and not level; there are no tubes under the bars; a stroke on bars that still ring waits up to half a swing of each bar and tops every mode up to a fresh stroke's level, which keeps a repeated key steady and lets the beat carry on; modes that would lie over 16 kHz or 0.45 of the sample rate are left out. Added because the level rules need it: with sixteen voices the sum of the bars is turned down by the root of the number of full strokes' worth of low tone that rings, past one.
